title: Denosumab for Obesity: A Multicenter RCT
abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity represents a significant cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, affecting millions of patients annually. Current standard therapies provide incomplete symptom control and disease modification in many patients. Denosumab has emerged as a promising therapeutic option based on its mechanism of action targeting key pathophysiological pathways involved in obesity. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter rct involving 2,500 participants with confirmed obesity (mean age 58 years, 43% male). Participants were randomized to receive either denosumab or standard care. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included safety outcomes, patient-reported quality of life, and subgroup analyses by age, sex, and disease severity. Median follow-up was 18 months. RESULTS: Treatment with denosumab resulted in a 21% relative improvement in all-cause mortality versus standard care (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-0.93, p<0.001). The absolute risk reduction was 29 percentage points (NNT = 14). Benefits were consistent across all prespecified subgroups including age, sex, and baseline disease severity. Adverse events were reported in 34% of the treatment group versus 29% of controls, most commonly mild and self-limiting. Serious adverse events occurred in 9% and 6% respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Denosumab demonstrates clinically meaningful and statistically significant efficacy for obesity, with an acceptable safety profile. These findings support the incorporation of denosumab into evidence-based treatment algorithms for appropriately selected patients. Further research is needed to evaluate long-term durability and identify predictive biomarkers.
